executive_summary: Target Corporation trades at 6.1x EV/EBITDA versus a peer median of 15.3x (WMT, COST, DG, KR) [E1]. One-year TSR of -38% trails the peer median of 23% [E12], while the FCF yield of 10.9% is well above peers [E3]. Institutional money is rotating out of the stock and into peers with lighter risk disclosure [E41]. The activist vulnerability score is 61.7/100 (high) [E40]. Insiders are buying in the open market [E38], and the capital-return model favors repurchases over a special dividend [E39]. Leverage should stay near current levels because the rating commitment is the binding constraint [E37]. The priority is to resume buybacks, address the top investor concerns with hard KPIs on the next call, and pre-empt activist pressure with a dated investor day.

recommendations.title: Capital structure: stay within the rating commitment
recommendations.action: Hold leverage near 28.0% debt/capital: the A rating commitment, not the cost of capital, is the binding constraint (optimum within the floor is 30.0%). Fund capital returns from free cash flow and working capital, and refinance maturities at the long end.
recommendations.rationale: Net debt/EBITDA is 1.31x vs a peer median of 1.35x [E8]; the WACC curve shows 7.87% today vs 7.84% at the constrained optimum [E37]. Management has tied leverage to its ratings commitment [E31, E28].
risks: EBIT decline compresses coverage faster than modeled
agency lease adjustments differ from the calibration offset

recommendations.title: Resume repurchases now; no special dividend
recommendations.action: Restart the buyback at ~$4.09bn per year from existing authorization. Front-load: execute ~40% of the year-one buyback via an accelerated share repurchase (ASR) to capture the current discount, and run the balance through a 10b5-1 grid that buys more below the 52-week VWAP. Keep the regular dividend; earmark ~$0.22bn for dividend growth. Next earnings expected around 2025-11-19; open-market purchases outside a 10b5-1 plan should stop ~2025-10-22 (quarter-end blackout) and resume 2 trading days after the release.
recommendations.rationale: Shares trade at a 60% EV/EBITDA discount to peers [E1, E39]. Even after haircutting the 10.9% FCF yield to 9.1% for the consensus EPS decline, the implied return on repurchased stock is 11.1% vs a 9.6% cost of equity [E39]. Insiders are buying in the open market (4 buyers, cluster=True) [E38]. Repurchases were paused while authorization remains [E32, E30].

recommendations.action: Run a pre-emptive 'activist audit' this quarter: (a) meet the top holders adding to positions and any activist on the register before the proxy nomination window; (b) announce a dated investor day with a multi-year margin and capital-return framework; (c) review board skills for retail operations and capital allocation; (d) prepare a fact base on the valuation gap and the turnaround milestones.

recommendations.title: Release working capital to fund returns

recommendations.title: M&A posture: no large deals at a trough multiple
recommendations.action: Avoid stock-funded or large debt-funded acquisitions while the shares trade at a discount; limit M&A to bolt-ons that accelerate digital, advertising or supply-chain capability and fit inside the rating floor. Publicly rebut unsupported market chatter with the stated capital-allocation order.
recommendations.rationale: Using undervalued stock as currency transfers value to sellers [E1], and leverage headroom within the rating floor is limited [E37]. Low-authority market chatter about a debt-funded deal or a dividend cut conflicts with management's stated priorities [E42, E31].
risks: missing a capability that peers acquire
